scope: Theorem 1 (Unit-charge Coulomb hardness) of the manuscript “QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy with unit nuclear charges” (preprints/QMA-hardness-of-continuum-Coulomb-energy-with-unit-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/QMA-hardness-of-continuum-Coulomb-energy-with-unit-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 275 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d817c071169eb58c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The electronic promise problem for (H) on HN , with distinct rational nuclear positions, all nuclear charges equal to one, unary electron number, and ratio- nal thresholds separated by at least L−1, is QMA-hard under deterministic classical polynomial-time many-one reductions. The reduction produces polynomially many nuclei and electrons, polynomial rational bit lengths, and threshold separation at least one. The only output data are the nuclear positions, electron number, and thresholds.
